scope: Read-only raw-result and saved-array interpretation; no planning, GPU or geometry rerun
interpretations: Each method has 180 legal dev attempts from 60 tasks, 20 scene clusters and three paired seeds. The independent random environments are the scene clusters, not the 180 repeated attempts.
The four local pipelines share 70 frontend failures and 110 validated DRM seeds. Failure to find a path in a fixed 6000-node graph is not proof that the continuous planning problem is infeasible.

CHOMP has one returned optimizer failure: line_search_stationary after 25 iterations, with solver_success=false. Its separately saved common validation rejects seven colliding samples outside the contact band; this is neither a crash nor a timeout. Native cost and path length improved, but the rejected path is excluded from successful quality statistics.

RRTConnect has one Exact solution candidate whose two colliding samples lie inside the fixed 2 micrometre contact band. Both collision implementations agree; validation_undetermined reflects contact ambiguity, not a checker disagreement, endpoint error, or sampling-step violation.

All 33 RRTConnect and 60 RRT* dev planner_timeout cases returned Approximate solution under the frozen 10-second search cap. They did not meet the exact-goal acceptance contract. They are not outer 60-second watchdog timeouts and do not establish infeasibility.

TrajOpt has 13 final collision failures despite returned candidates: 12 native CONVERGED and one PENALTY_ITERATION_LIMIT. All have collision samples outside the contact band and zero native/independent disagreements. Solver convergence is not a continuous-collision certificate.

TrajOpt has six validated nonconverged dev incumbents (five PENALTY_ITERATION_LIMIT and one SCO_ITERATION_LIMIT). These remain distinguished from native convergence; only common numerical validation qualifies them as successful outputs.

The comparison includes only the four newly frozen smoke/dev runs. Prior formal-test and historical baseline results are excluded. The test manifest remains protected; no new test planner evidence is present.

Collision acceptance is based on finite recorded sampling at 0.005 rad, not mathematical continuous collision freedom. All methods share a 60-second outer process limit, while declared internal iteration/search caps differ and remain frozen.

raw_termination_interpretation: Main metrics intentionally use top-level candidate termination/solver_status/native_status and explicit solver_converged only. CHOMP/STOMP candidates lack these top-level termination fields and solver_converged boolean, so their candidate termination/convergence remain unknown in frozen metrics. Raw optimizer_result.stop_reason supplies the actual stop/return reason below; line_search_stationary, relative_cost_tolerance, maximum_iterations and native_STOMP_return are not retroactively translated into convergence claims.
shared_frontend_failure_interpretation: Of the 70 shared dev frontend failures, 50 have the retained native no-path-in-roadmap exception and 20 are a normal native return with query_success=false. Neither establishes continuous-space infeasibility.
